scope: Committed presentation catalogs, bounded first-month continuity, the current live facility/operational-overlay/terminal-debrief/event-cue/music-state/history/replay/checkpoint bindings, and the current supported screenshot surface; not full-campaign raster or screenshot completion.

evidence: Every current catalog ID has a direct visible host condition and source/equivalent text.
Raw demand, access, staffed-bed, and pending-process overlays remain raw metrics without inferred categories.
The Rust fixture and browser tests cover all IDs, absence behavior, generic fallback, and the unchanged client authority boundary.
Every file-backed catalog entry declares a source SVG and release SVG.
Every file-backed catalog entry maps exactly once to an approved visual registry entry.
Registry and release-manifest/hash validators remain required release gates.

approval_contract: Every current visual and audio entry is approved.
IDs are unique within each registry and required fields are complete.
Provenance, license, accessible-equivalent, visible-source, and hash checks pass.

release_boundary.rule: File-backed entries require approved release paths and manifest hashes; runtime-generated or catalog/documentation entries retain null release paths.

limits: No future campaign asset inventory or placement/use claim is made.
Registry validity does not establish visual/audio quality, screenshot coverage, accessibility, or human review.
Runtime-generated audio and non-release GUI sources are not claimed to be file-backed release assets.
evidence: Current visual and audio registries pass schema, provenance, license, path, hash, security, and approval validation.
The release manifest covers every current non-null release path and credits projections are generated deterministically.

browser_smoke.result: The live viewport rendered executive metrics, briefing, campaign controls, accessibility settings, and the first-month path together.
browser_smoke.capture_policy: A viewport screenshot was inspected in the local browser and is not persisted as a golden raster artifact.

limits: No full-campaign state-by-state screenshot suite is claimed.
No committed PNG/JPEG golden, cross-browser matrix, or device capture is claimed.
Structural and SVG evidence does not establish pixel-level visual quality, accessibility quality, or human comprehension.
Future campaign placement/use, asset/audio quality, and human review remain separate gates.
evidence: All named current surfaces resolve to existing GUI sources and focused regression/structural tests.
The deterministic regional SVG snapshot remains stable and the local browser smoke route renders the current actor-visible desktop.
The browser remains read-only for simulation authority; screenshot inspection does not create or infer hidden state.
Event-channel catalog IDs equal the host projection and visible legacy fallback IDs exactly once.
Every event cue retains visible trigger-source, text-equivalent, and cues-only metadata.
Explicit empty host lists and unknown cue IDs remain non-authoritative presentation outcomes.

debrief_view_coverage.debrief_contract: Host-authored written debrief lines rendered as text
terminal_behavior: Valid envelope renders history, replay metadata, and debrief together.
Successful terminal render disables further session action controls.
Optional debrief audio remains atmospheric and written text remains complete.
failure_behavior: Unknown schema, invalid replay count, hash/count mismatch, or incomplete envelope fails closed.
Invalid terminal data does not mutate the current presentation into a completed state.
debrief_view_coverage.boundary: Host/core owns history, replay metadata, and debrief facts; the browser validates and renders only the supplied terminal projection.
evidence: The live terminal test covers schema validation, row rendering, hash/count alignment, terminal controls, failure rejection, route/source markers, and syntax.
No instructor-only, counterfactual, durable persistence, replay-regeneration, human-usability, or learning claim is made.

continuity_behavior: Host stores and restores one cloned checkpoint per active session.
Restore returns aligned loaded metadata without entering a new transition.
Browser refreshes actor-visible presentation after successful restore.
Missing checkpoint, adapter, or refresh failure preserves a recoverable current view.
checkpoint_view_coverage.boundary: Host/core owns checkpoint state and restore; the browser receives metadata and refreshes read-only projections without serializing true state.
limits: No durable file persistence or browser storage is established.
No cross-process or browser-refresh recovery is established.
No replay regeneration, playback, screenshot, accessibility, or human-learning claim is made.
evidence: The live checkpoint test covers schema/operation/hash/count validation, adapter save/load, refresh, missing/failure recovery, controls/routes, syntax, and authority exclusions.
Rust session tests cover cloned host restore and aligned replay metadata without a new transition.

continuity_behavior: Host returns immutable visible transition summaries without entering a new transition.
Replay metadata aligns seed, transition count, latest state hash, and visible rows.
Browser renders the projection through the existing text-first history surface.
Missing adapter, failed read, or malformed replay preserves the last valid view and exposes a recoverable error.
replay_view_coverage.boundary: Host/core owns replay metadata, immutable history, and state hashes; the browser validates and renders a read-only projection without playback, regeneration, or client authority.
limits: No replay playback or regenerated simulation trace is established.
No durable replay persistence or browser-authored hash is established.
No screenshot, accessibility, usability, or human-learning claim is made.
evidence: The live replay test covers schema/operation-independent metadata validation, empty and committed views, adapter fallback, rendering, failure preservation, route/source markers, syntax, and authority exclusions.
Rust session, MCP, and transport tests cover immutable history alignment and the read-only replay route.
Every catalog state has visible source, text equivalent, fallback, and ordered stem metadata.
The host projection emits only the six resolution states; menu remains an explicit browser stage.
Classifier priority and unknown-state fallback remain visible-only and deterministic.

history_view_coverage.failure_behavior: Keep the last valid history view and expose a recoverable adapter error.
evidence: Valid history requires aligned transition_count and transition rows with state hashes.
Unsupported schemas, incomplete counts, missing adapters, and thrown reads fail closed without simulation access.
The GUI route and browser validator reject noncompetitive sessions for this bounded history schema.
The history read path remains read-only and cannot submit commands or expose hidden state.

browser_refresh_coverage.host_read_source: Existing getSession, presentation, action-catalog, and campaign-coverage reads
browser_refresh_coverage.stored_value: One opaque non-empty host-issued session ID only
continuity_behavior: Successful host start/load stores the session ID and prefills the existing-session control.
A fresh page attempts the existing host-owned load path when the same host process is still running.
Confirmed unknown-session failures clear the stale ID; other failures preserve it for retry.
Successful host end clears the ID; blocked storage never blocks a session or written fallback.
browser_refresh_coverage.boundary: Browser storage is best-effort presentation state; the host remains authoritative for sessions, transitions, history, replay, checkpoints, and outcomes.
limits: No durable file persistence, browser serialization, or cross-process recovery is established.
No replay playback/regeneration, screenshot, device, accessibility, usability, or human-learning claim is made.
evidence: Focused tests cover safe storage, successful and failed start/load, refresh recovery, stale cleanup, end cleanup, written fallback, and forbidden authority markers.
The existing host process remains in-memory; a stopped or restarted host makes the stored ID unavailable and does not create a replacement session.

continuity.boundary: History, debrief, replay, save/load, hashes, cue authority, music-state authority, and transition authority remain host/core-owned; the live history, replay, checkpoint, terminal, event-cue, and music-state slices verify host responses and presentation references only.

open_limits: Full competitive-campaign facility placement and usage coverage is not established by this bounded ledger; the facility asset catalog and release registry are complete, while live bindings cover only directly supported current player conditions.
Durable file persistence, browser serialization, and cross-process recovery are not established by the same-host browser-refresh slice.
No screenshot suite, performance benchmark, low-power device test, browser compatibility matrix, or human quality finding is recorded.
Catalog presence and fallback semantics do not establish asset quality, accessibility quality, audio usefulness, legal clearance, or educational benefit.
